Impact at a glance

Why we exist

What happens to the poor?

Health Leads Initiative was founded in January 2019 by a group of young people led by Dr Charles Nwachukwu.

During his medical internship in Nigeria, Dr Nwachukwu saw a troubling pattern: people with some financial means could usually find a way to get care when they needed it, while many others could not.

It raised a question that continues to drive our work: What happens to the poor?

HLI exists to help answer that question by working alongside communities, local health workers, and partners to make healthcare more accessible, regardless of income or background.

About Health Leads Initiative

A commitment to healthcare for all.

Founded by young people in 2019, Health Leads Initiative works to make healthcare more accessible to underserved populations across Africa.

Our story

Why Health Leads Initiative exists

Health Leads Initiative was founded in January 2019 by a group of young people led by Dr Charles Nwachukwu.

During his medical internship in Nigeria, Dr Nwachukwu saw a troubling pattern: people with some financial means could usually find a way to get care when they needed it, while many others could not.

What happens to the poor?

HLI exists to help answer that question by working alongside communities, local health workers, and partners to make healthcare more accessible, regardless of income or background.

Our mission

Healthcare regardless of status

To increase healthcare accessibility for underserved populations in Africa, regardless of their socioeconomic status.

Our vision

An Africa without barriers

An Africa where no one goes without healthcare because they cannot afford it.

Founder

Dr Charles Nwachukwu's experience during his medical internship in Nigeria brought him face-to-face with the unequal realities of healthcare access. He observed that people with financial resources could often find a way to obtain care, while others struggled to access the same services.

The question, ‘What happens to the poor?’ became a defining motivation for the establishment of Health Leads Initiative in January 2019, alongside a group of young people committed to expanding healthcare access.
